findings.evidence: reconcile() raises ValueError('account_position_mismatch') whenever any locally held symbol's remote holding_quantity differs. That raise leaves reconcile() on the first statement inside cycle()'s try (runtime.py:99), is caught by the blanket handler at runtime.py:389, and returns blocked - so the position-protection loop at runtime.py:169 never executes. Reproduced with Runtime.cycle() and the in-repo Client fixture, quote bid far below stop: (A) local{005930:1}/remote{005930:1} -> running, sell/stop/1 placed; (B) local{005930:2}/remote{005930:1} -> blocked, 0 sells; (C) local{005930:1}/remote{005930:2} -> blocked, 0 sells; (D) local{005930:1}/remote{005930:1,000660:3} -> protecting, sell placed, incident=account_exposure_unattributed; (E) local{005930:1,000660:1}/remote{005930:1,000660:5} -> blocked, 0 sells although 005930 matches exactly. A second probe ran three cycles (all blocked, 0 sells), issued store.control('flatten') (control becomes 'flattening'), then three more cycles - still blocked, still 0 sells, positions [('000660',1),('005930',1)] still held. The flatten branch lives at runtime.py:177-193, downstream of the raise, so the operator's emergency liquidation control is unreachable.
findings.proposal: Replace the raise at broker.py:142-143 with the same soft-fail path already used for remote supersets: store.put('reconciliation_reason','account_position_mismatch') and let the function return False. New entries stay blocked via runtime.py:100-106 and :230, while the protection loop keeps running for every position. Selling more than the broker actually holds is already fail-closed per order at broker.py:193-197 (remote.orderable_quantity < order['quantity'] -> broker_sell_quantity_unavailable), so the cycle-wide raise is redundant defence bought at the price of all protective exits. Add a regression test alongside test_paper_review_regressions.py:70 covering shape (E) - one matched symbol plus one divergent symbol must still place the matched symbol's stop.

findings.evidence: unmanaged is computed by matching every get_cancelable_orders() row against every dispatch with _cancel_identity_matches, which requires row.total_filled_quantity == int(dispatch.cumulative_filled_quantity) and Decimal(row.total_filled_amount) == sum(fill_evidence notional) (paper_kill.py:578-579). reconcile_unresolved() (broker.py:111) and get_cancelable_orders() (broker.py:157) are separate KIS endpoints at least 1.05s apart via LimitedTransport, so a partial fill of our own order between the two calls makes the row advance past the dispatch, no dispatch matches, and unmanaged becomes True. reconcile then returns False and runtime.py:161-167 raises the incident code 'external_working_order' for an order that is entirely ours.
findings.proposal: Distinguish the cases: when a row matches a dispatch on identity fields (order_number, branch, symbol, side, quantity) but only the fill-state equalities differ, emit a separate reason such as 'own_order_fill_state_advancing' instead of 'external_working_order'. The soft-fail behaviour is correct; only the operator-facing code is wrong.

findings.evidence: snapshot() builds candidate_status as {s: store.get('candidate_status:' + s, 'ready') for s in store.get('universe', [])}. The collector refreshes the universe independently (collector.py:34-38), so a symbol it has just added has no candidate_status key until the order loop's per-symbol pass at runtime.py:275-293 runs. Until then the operator report claims 'ready' for a symbol that has never been evaluated, and the same holds for any cycle that returns early at runtime.py:231 ('protecting').
findings.proposal: Change the default from 'ready' to 'not_evaluated' so an absent key is reported as unknown rather than as the healthiest possible state.

findings.evidence: bounded_run(command, *, timeout, env, max_output_bytes=65536, **kwargs) swallows every extra keyword. lab.py:890-903 and :908-916 pass capture_output=True, text=False, check=False and shell=False expecting subprocess.run semantics; all four are discarded. Today the outcomes coincide (bounded_run always captures, always returns bytes, never raises on returncode, never uses a shell), so the behaviour is correct by accident, but a future caller passing check=True would silently get no exception on a nonzero exit.
findings.proposal: Either consume the supported keywords explicitly and honour check, or raise TypeError on unexpected keywords so a semantic mismatch fails loudly instead of being ignored.

findings.evidence: The worker branch imports SlackDM but calls work_once(store) with no sender, so jobs.py:11-12 and :93-94 never drain the outbox from the worker. Delivery happens only in the separate reporter process (cli.py:149-162), which is the intended design, leaving the import dead.
findings.proposal: Drop the import so the worker/reporter split stays legible.

findings.evidence: test_unrelated_holding_blocks_entries_but_preserves_known_stop only covers a remote superset by an unrelated ticker (000660), which is exactly the shape that passes; the quantity-divergence branch at broker.py:142 - the one that strands protection - has no test, which is why BLOCK-1 survived. test_paper_collector calls Collector.collect_once directly on the main thread, so the background thread with its own SQLite connection running concurrently with a cycle is never exercised. The alternate-provider generation retry at research.py:211-217 has no test either (the reviewer-independence derivation at :245 is correct on inspection but unverified after a retry).
findings.proposal: Add: (1) a regression test for one matched plus one divergent symbol asserting the matched symbol's stop is still placed; (2) a collector test that starts the real thread against a live cycle and asserts no SQLite locking error and consistent bars; (3) a research test where the primary provider returns LabError and the alternate succeeds, asserting the reviewer provider is the opposite of source.provider.

unresolvedRisks: Deliberately excluded from this review and therefore unverified: real network calls, manual KIS paper sessions, Slack delivery, live AI provider adapters, and Docker sandbox execution. run_signal_code, verify_sandbox_readiness and the lab container lifecycle were read and reasoned about but never executed against a real Docker daemon, so container-escape and image-pinning behaviour rest on code inspection only.

The DurablePaperSubmissionCoordinator is constructed once per begin() with a snapshot of RefreshingClient.current_client() (broker.py:68-78), while submit()'s other calls (get_buying_power, get_balance, get_cancelable_orders) go through the auto-renewing proxy. Because begin() runs at the top of every cycle the staleness window is bounded by cycle_seconds (default 10s) against a ~24h token, so this is safe as written - but it becomes a live 401 risk if begin() is ever hoisted out of the per-cycle path.

reconcile() issues two get_balance() calls per invocation (broker.py:112 and :136) and runtime.cycle() calls reconcile twice (runtime.py:99 and :161), so a cycle spends at least four balance reads plus cancelable-order reads on the shared 1.05s LimitedTransport budget, concurrently with the collector thread. Request-budget headroom under a full 20-symbol universe was not measured and could throttle the protection loop on a real account.

store.verify_cash() and the reconcile raises are hard aborts that skip position protection for the whole cycle. Even after BLOCK-1 is fixed for the position path, experiment_cash_ledger_mismatch (store.py:182) retains the same all-or-nothing shape and has no operator remediation command.

Two SQLite writers (main cycle and collector thread) share the experiment DB with a 15s busy timeout under WAL. No sustained concurrent-write soak was run, so lock contention under a full trading session is unmeasured.
